newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVENERGO TO BE HOLDING COMPANY IN JAN 1998.
newsitem.headline: LATVENERGO TO BE HOLDING COMPANY IN JAN 1998.

text.p: The privatisation agency (LPA) said on Wednesday that Latvenergo, the state electricity firm, will become a holding company from January 1998 and strategic investors will be able to buy into it from the end of the year.

"The agency has approved the sale guidelines for Latvenergo which will be turned into a concern with four daughter companies-generators in competition with each other," Janis Naglis, LPA director general, told a news conference.
He said that strategic investors may be allowed to buy a stake at the end of this year.
"We have already had interest expressed from German Preussen Elektra and Belan, the joint electricity company of Berlin," said Edgars Birkans, Latvenergo manager.
Naglis said the actual rules for the sale of Latvenergo will be drawn up after the state electricity price regulator has made its recommendations on competition.

The guidelines for the Latvenergo sale foresee two hydroelectric power companies formed from the Daugava cascade, generators Plavinas and Kegums and the Riga hyrdro-electric power station, also on the Daugava river, forming another.
Two more companies will be set up from the thermoelectric power stations TEC-1 and TEC-2.
The grid will have the function of only buyer for the generated power and will operate the transmission system.
"Latvenergo daughter companies are already operating this year as separate profit centres and our grid has long been working as a separate entity," Birkans added.
"But we still have to introduce metering of active and reactive power between the daughter companies. We have that in place already on the border with Russia, Estonia and Lithuiania," he added.
